# MCP tools reference

`cloudseed setup mcp` turns cloudseed into a Model Context Protocol server with **30 tools**, **12 resources** and **4 prompts**. Tools marked *confirm* change infrastructure, a host or a service (or can print secrets): the server refuses them unless the call carries `confirm=true`, which a client may only send after you agreed. See the [MCP guide](../guides/mcp.md).

!!! info "Generated from the code"
    This page is generated by `scripts/gen-docs.py` from the MCP server's own tool list (`cloudseed/mcp.py`), so it always matches the CLI you install (this build: cloudseed 0.1.0).

## Tools

| Tool | Confirm | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| [`cloudseed_list`](#cloudseed_list) | – | List all environments (cloud, region, state, bastion IP, working dir). |
| [`cloudseed_doctor`](#cloudseed_doctor) | – | Check tools, versions and cloud credentials. With a cloud it exits 1 when that cloud is not ready (a required tool missing or too old, no or invalid credentials; the last line says what); without one it always exits 0. |
| [`cloudseed_setup`](#cloudseed_setup) | some uses | Create or update an environment (network, bastion, baseline; optional Kubernetes/VPN). Shows the plan; apply=true applies it; dry\_run=true only renders and validates. A plan creates nothing in the cloud: a new remote-state bucket/container is only planned then (with a throw-away local state) and created first on apply. Without apply nothing is kept either (like `cs setup --preview`): an existing environment keeps its saved configuration and a new one is not created, so the same call with apply=true applies what was shown. save=true instead keeps the planned settings for a later cloudseed\_apply (like `cs setup --plan-only`; no undo point is recorded for them). Renaming a deployed environment (name) needs that: setup never applies a rename unattended, so plan it with save=true, show the plan, then call cloudseed\_apply. To price an environment before creating it, call this with dry\_run=true first (offline, no cloud credentials, saves its settings, creates nothing), then cloudseed\_finops action=estimate; a plan without apply keeps nothing to estimate. Only apply=true needs confirm=true (a plan or dry\_run does not). |
| [`cloudseed_plan`](#cloudseed_plan) | – | Show what apply would change. |
| [`cloudseed_apply`](#cloudseed_apply) | always | Apply the saved configuration (creates/changes cloud resources), including settings saved by an earlier cloudseed\_setup call with save=true; call cloudseed\_plan first to see what it would change. Needs confirm=true (ask the user first). |
| [`cloudseed_destroy`](#cloudseed_destroy) | always | Destroy everything in an environment, or only the given Terraform targets (cloudseed\_inventory lists the addresses). Targets that match nothing in the state are skipped with a warning; when none matches, nothing is changed and the call fails (exit code 1). purge\_state / purge apply to a full destroy only. Needs confirm=true (ask the user first). |
| [`cloudseed_status`](#cloudseed_status) | – | Configuration, state summary, outputs and next steps of an environment. |
| [`cloudseed_output`](#cloudseed_output) | – | Stack outputs as JSON (bastion IP, subnet IDs, cluster endpoint...), returned on their own: notes and warnings follow separately. |
| [`cloudseed_update_ip`](#cloudseed_update_ip) | always | Re-detect the public IP (or use allow\_ip) and apply the new bastion SSH allow-list. Cloud targets (aws, gcp, azure) only: not applicable to vmware (its VMs sit on a private VMware network this machine reaches directly; a vmware call changes nothing). Needs confirm=true (ask the user first). |
| [`cloudseed_ssh`](#cloudseed_ssh) | always | Run a shell command on the bastion over SSH (non-interactive) and return its output. Needs confirm=true (ask the user first). |
| [`cloudseed_provision`](#cloudseed_provision) | always | Copy the repo to the bastion/VPN/k8s nodes and run the Ansible hardening/tooling (as root on the hosts). Needs confirm=true (ask the user first). |
| [`cloudseed_inventory`](#cloudseed_inventory) | – | What exists in the environment (from state) and its change history. |
| [`cloudseed_troubleshoot`](#cloudseed_troubleshoot) | – | Deterministic diagnosis: audit log, last failure, inventory, reachability, tools. |
| [`cloudseed_explain`](#cloudseed_explain) | – | Explain how anything in cloudseed works: a feature (vpn, kubernetes, dr), a target (aws, gcp, azure, vmware), a command (destroy), a topic (envs), a platform group or item (security, istio) or a setup variable. A bare word is looked up as feature &gt; target &gt; platform group/item &gt; command/topic; the namespaced forms pick one meaning: 'feature vpn', 'target vmware', 'command vpn', 'topic security', 'group security', 'item velero', 'platform &lt;group&#124;item&gt;', 'variables aws', 'variable aws single\_nat\_gateway' (or 'aws single\_nat\_gateway'). format=json returns the page as data (kind, title, summary, sections, commands, also, did\_you\_mean); the same data is the resource cloudseed://explain/{query}. |
| [`cloudseed_help`](#cloudseed_help) | – | cloudseed help pages: command, topic, 'variables &lt;cloud&gt;', 'outputs &lt;cloud&gt;' (or topic=variables with cloud=aws). |
| [`cloudseed_k8s`](#cloudseed_k8s) | – | Kubernetes info for the environment's cluster; tunnel/untunnel open/close an SSH tunnel to a private API. kubeconfig merges the cluster into the user's own kubeconfig ($KUBECONFIG's first file, else ~/.kube/config) AND makes it the current kubectl context, so kubectl in every terminal of the user targets it from then on (the other contexts are kept; cloudseed\_undo reverts it). cloudseed\_kubectl/cloudseed\_helm never need it (they use a per-environment kubeconfig): tell the user before calling it. |
| [`cloudseed_node`](#cloudseed_node) | some uses | Scale the cluster: list nodes, add N nodes, remove a node, or (EKS/GKE/AKS) set the managed pool size and autoscaler limits with scale. Add, remove and scale need confirm=true (list does not). |
| [`cloudseed_platform`](#cloudseed_platform) | some uses | Platform catalog: list/status/plan/info/install/uninstall groups (basek8s scaling data ai agentic finops devsecops security resilience chaos) or items (cloud prerequisites such as buckets/identities are applied first); ui exposes installed UIs. Install, uninstall and ui need confirm=true (list, status, plan and info do not). |
| [`cloudseed_kubectl`](#cloudseed_kubectl) | some uses | Run kubectl against the cluster of the environment picked by cloud and/or env (either one alone works; neither = the current environment, cs env use, or the only cluster). Over MCP it runs without a terminal and returns its whole output at the end, so commands that never end are refused: follow/watch (logs -f, get -w), port-forward, proxy and attach; use logs --tail=200 or --since=10m, get without -w, or kubectl wait --for=condition=... --timeout=120s. Interactive ones (edit, exec/run/debug -i/-t) are refused too: those belong in the user's own terminal. Reads run directly (get, describe, logs, top, explain, version, api-resources, api-versions, cluster-info, events); everything else needs confirm=true, a get of Secrets included, and so do get --raw (except the health, version and metrics endpoints), get/describe -f/-k, -o \*-file, cluster-info dump --output-directory, any option that points kubectl at another server, identity or local file (--server, --kubeconfig, --context, --token, --as, --insecure-skip-tls-verify ...) and an option before the verb that cloudseed cannot read. |
| [`cloudseed_helm`](#cloudseed_helm) | some uses | Run helm against the cluster of the environment picked by cloud and/or env (either one alone works; neither = the current environment, cs env use, or the only cluster). Reads run directly (list, status with table output, history, show, search, version, env, repo/dependency/plugin list, get notes/metadata); everything else needs confirm=true, including the reads that carry release secrets: status -o json/yaml and get values/all/manifest/hooks, template/lint (they render charts with values and files from this machine), and any option that points helm at another server, identity or local file (--kube-apiserver, --kube-context, --kubeconfig, --kube-token ...). |
| [`cloudseed_vpn`](#cloudseed_vpn) | some uses | VPN: status, users, add-user, revoke, provision. Add-user, revoke and provision need confirm=true (status and users do not). |
| [`cloudseed_finops`](#cloudseed_finops) | – | Costs: estimate (offline), cloud bill, Kubernetes allocation (OpenCost), or a saved report. estimate prices a saved environment from its settings and inventory: for one that does not exist yet, call cloudseed\_setup with dry\_run=true first (offline, no credentials, creates nothing), then estimate. |
| [`cloudseed_env`](#cloudseed_env) | – | Show or set the current environment for cluster commands (an id alone means use). |
| [`cloudseed_managed`](#cloudseed_managed) | some uses | Databricks / Snowflake: status, test, or pass a CLI command (profile per environment: env, or cloud + env, picks the environment whose profile is used; neither = the current environment's, else 'default'). Status, test and plain list/get/describe commands run directly; anything else (sql, connect, create, delete, ...) needs confirm=true. |
| [`cloudseed_chaos`](#cloudseed_chaos) | some uses | Chaos engineering: list experiments, run a suite/experiments (installs Chaos Mesh, prints PASS/FAIL), status, stop, last report. Run and stop need confirm=true (list, status and report do not). |
| [`cloudseed_dr`](#cloudseed_dr) | some uses | Disaster recovery (Velero): status, backups, backup, restore, schedule, the automated drill `test` (create/backup/delete/restore/verify), or velero's own view of one backup/restore: describe (details=true lists every object and volume) and logs. Backup, restore, schedule and test need confirm=true (status, backups, describe and logs do not). |
| [`cloudseed_scan`](#cloudseed_scan) | some uses | Scans with saved reports: architecture (AWS/Azure/GCP Well-Architected screening, common guidance for VMware; local configuration and saved evidence only, no live cloud checks), cis (kube-bench), kube (kubescape NSA/MITRE), images (trivy), host (OpenSCAP CIS), stig (DISA STIG), cloud (prowler CIS), fips (FIPS 140 verification), all (security scans only), reports. Architecture returns PASS, FAIL, or INCOMPLETE when required evidence is missing or stale. Every kind except architecture, fips and reports runs cluster jobs or Ansible on hosts and needs confirm=true; a scanner missing on this machine is never installed by an MCP call (it stops with the install command for the user). |
| [`cloudseed_undo`](#cloudseed_undo) | some uses | Undo the newest state-changing action of an environment (fifteen kept per environment, at most five of one kind): restores the previous configuration and re-applies, uninstalls what was installed, revokes, deletes backups... list=true shows the history with entry ids; pass cloud (+ env), or the id of the newest entry of an environment. drop=true discards that entry without undoing it (for a step that can never succeed). Global actions (MCP/UI/credential/agent settings) can only be undone by the user (cs undo --global in a terminal, or the web console's Undo): an agent's call is refused. Everything except list=true needs confirm=true. |
| [`cloudseed_install`](#cloudseed_install) | always | Install a tool or group cloudseed needs: terraform aws gcloud az kubectl helm k9s openvpn tailscale go qemu-img vmware-provider &#124; cloud vmware vpn. Needs confirm=true (ask the user first). |
| [`cloudseed_skill`](#cloudseed_skill) | – | Read one of the bundled agent skills (cloudseed, cloudseed-aws/gcp/azure/vmware, cloudseed-destroy, cloudseed-platform, ...): the operating manual for driving cloudseed. |

### cloudseed_doctor

Check tools, versions and cloud credentials. With a cloud it exits 1 when that cloud is not ready (a required tool missing or too old, no or invalid credentials; the last line says what); without one it always exits 0.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cloud` | `aws` \| `gcp` \| `azure` \| `vmware` |  | target: aws &#124; gcp &#124; azure &#124; vmware |

### cloudseed_setup

Create or update an environment (network, bastion, baseline; optional Kubernetes/VPN). Shows the plan; apply=true applies it; dry\_run=true only renders and validates. A plan creates nothing in the cloud: a new remote-state bucket/container is only planned then (with a throw-away local state) and created first on apply. Without apply nothing is kept either (like `cs setup --preview`): an existing environment keeps its saved configuration and a new one is not created, so the same call with apply=true applies what was shown. save=true instead keeps the planned settings for a later cloudseed\_apply (like `cs setup --plan-only`; no undo point is recorded for them). Renaming a deployed environment (name) needs that: setup never applies a rename unattended, so plan it with save=true, show the plan, then call cloudseed\_apply. To price an environment before creating it, call this with dry\_run=true first (offline, no cloud credentials, saves its settings, creates nothing), then cloudseed\_finops action=estimate; a plan without apply keeps nothing to estimate. Only apply=true needs confirm=true (a plan or dry\_run does not).

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cloud` | `aws` \| `gcp` \| `azure` \| `vmware` | yes | target: aws &#124; gcp &#124; azure &#124; vmware |
| `env` | string |  | environment name, e.g. dev (lowercase letters, digits, hyphens). Blank: the cloud's only environment, else the current one for read-only tools, else dev; tools that change things never guess |
| `name` | string |  |  |
| `region` | string |  |  |
| `state` | `remote` \| `local` |  |  |
| `cidr` | string |  |  |
| `allow_ip` | string |  |  |
| `vars` | object |  | stack variables to override, e.g. {"enable\_kubernetes": true}; null resets a saved override to its default. Variables cloudseed sets itself (name, region, network CIDRs, allowed\_ssh\_cidrs, tags/labels, ssh\_public\_key ...) are refused: use the dedicated fields (name, region, cidr, allow\_ip, tags) |
| `apply` | boolean |  | apply the plan (otherwise plan only: nothing is kept) |
| `save` | boolean |  | without apply: keep the planned settings for a later cloudseed\_apply (needed to rename a deployed environment) |
| `dry_run` | boolean |  | render + terraform validate only; touches nothing |
| `tags` | object |  | extra tags/labels on every resource, {key: value}; a key cannot be empty, contain '=' or start/end with a space |
| `workdir` | string |  |  |
| `project_id` | string |  |  |
| `subscription_id` | string |  |  |
| `profile` | string |  |  |
| `no_provision` | boolean |  | apply only: do not copy the repo to the bastion and harden it with Ansible |
| `no_harden` | boolean |  | provision without OS hardening; sshd settings, fail2ban, kernel/core-dump/sudo settings and audit rules from an earlier run are removed (PAM and umask edits stay; automatic updates are left as they are); the host firewall and IP forwarding stay (no\_firewall) |
| `no_firewall` | boolean |  | provision without the nftables host firewall (an earlier run's is removed; VPN/NAT hosts keep their NAT rule) |
| `no_tools` | boolean |  | provision without installing terraform / the cloud CLI on the bastion |
| `confirm` | boolean |  | must be true to run a destructive action (ask the user first) |

### cloudseed_destroy

Destroy everything in an environment, or only the given Terraform targets (cloudseed\_inventory lists the addresses). Targets that match nothing in the state are skipped with a warning; when none matches, nothing is changed and the call fails (exit code 1). purge\_state / purge apply to a full destroy only. Needs confirm=true (ask the user first).

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cloud` | `aws` \| `gcp` \| `azure` \| `vmware` | yes | target: aws &#124; gcp &#124; azure &#124; vmware |
| `env` | string |  | environment name, e.g. dev (lowercase letters, digits, hyphens). Blank: the cloud's only environment, else the current one for read-only tools, else dev; tools that change things never guess |
| `targets` | array of string |  | Terraform addresses to destroy only, e.g. module.stack.module.bastion (empty = everything) |
| `purge_state` | boolean |  | also delete the remote state bucket/container (irreversible) |
| `purge` | boolean |  | also delete the local env directory; config.json and the SSH keys are kept in the undo journal so cloudseed\_undo can re-create the environment, VPN keys are not |
| `confirm` | boolean |  | must be true to run a destructive action (ask the user first) |

### cloudseed_kubectl

Run kubectl against the cluster of the environment picked by cloud and/or env (either one alone works; neither = the current environment, cs env use, or the only cluster). Over MCP it runs without a terminal and returns its whole output at the end, so commands that never end are refused: follow/watch (logs -f, get -w), port-forward, proxy and attach; use logs --tail=200 or --since=10m, get without -w, or kubectl wait --for=condition=... --timeout=120s. Interactive ones (edit, exec/run/debug -i/-t) are refused too: those belong in the user's own terminal. Reads run directly (get, describe, logs, top, explain, version, api-resources, api-versions, cluster-info, events); everything else needs confirm=true, a get of Secrets included, and so do get --raw (except the health, version and metrics endpoints), get/describe -f/-k, -o \*-file, cluster-info dump --output-directory, any option that points kubectl at another server, identity or local file (--server, --kubeconfig, --context, --token, --as, --insecure-skip-tls-verify ...) and an option before the verb that cloudseed cannot read.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `args` | string | yes | kubectl arguments, e.g. 'get pods -A' (the cluster goes in cloud/env) |
| `cloud` | `aws` \| `gcp` \| `azure` \| `vmware` |  | target: aws &#124; gcp &#124; azure &#124; vmware |
| `env` | string |  | environment name, e.g. dev (lowercase letters, digits, hyphens). Blank: the cloud's only environment, else the current one for read-only tools, else dev; tools that change things never guess |
| `confirm` | boolean |  | must be true to run a destructive action (ask the user first) |

### cloudseed_helm

Run helm against the cluster of the environment picked by cloud and/or env (either one alone works; neither = the current environment, cs env use, or the only cluster). Reads run directly (list, status with table output, history, show, search, version, env, repo/dependency/plugin list, get notes/metadata); everything else needs confirm=true, including the reads that carry release secrets: status -o json/yaml and get values/all/manifest/hooks, template/lint (they render charts with values and files from this machine), and any option that points helm at another server, identity or local file (--kube-apiserver, --kube-context, --kubeconfig, --kube-token ...).

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `args` | string | yes | helm arguments, e.g. 'list -A' (the cluster goes in cloud/env) |
| `cloud` | `aws` \| `gcp` \| `azure` \| `vmware` |  | target: aws &#124; gcp &#124; azure &#124; vmware |
| `env` | string |  | environment name, e.g. dev (lowercase letters, digits, hyphens). Blank: the cloud's only environment, else the current one for read-only tools, else dev; tools that change things never guess |
| `confirm` | boolean |  | must be true to run a destructive action (ask the user first) |

### cloudseed_finops

Costs: estimate (offline), cloud bill, Kubernetes allocation (OpenCost), or a saved report. estimate prices a saved environment from its settings and inventory: for one that does not exist yet, call cloudseed\_setup with dry\_run=true first (offline, no credentials, creates nothing), then estimate.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | `estimate` \| `cloud` \| `k8s` \| `report` | yes |  |
| `cloud` | `aws` \| `gcp` \| `azure` \| `vmware` |  | target: aws &#124; gcp &#124; azure &#124; vmware |
| `env` | string |  | environment name, e.g. dev (lowercase letters, digits, hyphens). Blank: the cloud's only environment, else the current one for read-only tools, else dev; tools that change things never guess |
| `days` | integer |  | days of billing history (1-365) |
| `window` | string |  |  |
| `by` | string |  |  |
| `save` | boolean |  | also save the result as a report under &lt;workdir&gt;/finops/ (report always saves) |

Show or set the current environment for cluster commands (an id alone means use).

### cloudseed_managed

Databricks / Snowflake: status, test, or pass a CLI command (profile per environment: env, or cloud + env, picks the environment whose profile is used; neither = the current environment's, else 'default'). Status, test and plain list/get/describe commands run directly; anything else (sql, connect, create, delete, ...) needs confirm=true.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `service` | `databricks` \| `snowflake` | yes |  |
| `args` | string |  | CLI arguments, e.g. 'clusters list' (default: status) |
| `profile` | string |  | profile name (overrides the environment's) |
| `cloud` | `aws` \| `gcp` \| `azure` \| `vmware` |  | with env: the environment's cloud (aws &#124; gcp &#124; azure &#124; vmware), for a name several clouds use |
| `env` | string |  | the environment whose profile is used: a name (dev) or an id (aws-dev) |
| `confirm` | boolean |  | must be true to run a destructive action (ask the user first) |

### cloudseed_chaos

Chaos engineering: list experiments, run a suite/experiments (installs Chaos Mesh, prints PASS/FAIL), status, stop, last report. Run and stop need confirm=true (list, status and report do not).

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | `run` \| `list` \| `status` \| `stop` \| `report` | yes |  |
| `items` | array of string |  | suites (basic network stress full) or experiment names |
| `cloud` | `aws` \| `gcp` \| `azure` \| `vmware` |  | target: aws &#124; gcp &#124; azure &#124; vmware |
| `env` | string |  | environment name, e.g. dev (lowercase letters, digits, hyphens). Blank: the cloud's only environment, else the current one for read-only tools, else dev; tools that change things never guess |
| `target` | string |  | ns/deployment\[:port] to test a real workload |
| `duration` | integer |  | seconds per experiment (15-3600, default 45) |
| `replicas` | integer |  | run: canary replicas (2-20, default 3; not used with target) |
| `keep` | boolean |  | run: keep the canary namespace afterwards (chaos stop removes it) |
| `confirm` | boolean |  | must be true to run a destructive action (ask the user first) |

### cloudseed_dr

Disaster recovery (Velero): status, backups, backup, restore, schedule, the automated drill `test` (create/backup/delete/restore/verify), or velero's own view of one backup/restore: describe (details=true lists every object and volume) and logs. Backup, restore, schedule and test need confirm=true (status, backups, describe and logs do not).

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | `status` \| `backups` \| `backup` \| `restore` \| `schedule` \| `test` \| `describe` \| `logs` | yes |  |
| `name` | string |  |  |
| `cloud` | `aws` \| `gcp` \| `azure` \| `vmware` |  | target: aws &#124; gcp &#124; azure &#124; vmware |
| `env` | string |  | environment name, e.g. dev (lowercase letters, digits, hyphens). Blank: the cloud's only environment, else the current one for read-only tools, else dev; tools that change things never guess |
| `kind` | `backup` \| `restore` |  | describe/logs: what `name` is |
| `details` | boolean |  | describe: also list every object and volume (velero describe --details) |
| `namespaces` | string |  |  |
| `cron` | string |  |  |
| `ttl` | string |  | schedule: how long Velero keeps each backup, e.g. 720h, 72h30m or 30d (days are rewritten to hours: 30d = 720h; default 720h) |
| `no_wait` | boolean |  | backup/restore: return immediately instead of waiting for Velero |
| `keep` | boolean |  | test: keep the drill namespace and backup for inspection |
| `volume` | `` \| `on` \| `off` |  | test: force the volume backup on or off (blank = when a default StorageClass exists) |
| `confirm` | boolean |  | must be true to run a destructive action (ask the user first) |

### cloudseed_scan

Scans with saved reports: architecture (AWS/Azure/GCP Well-Architected screening, common guidance for VMware; local configuration and saved evidence only, no live cloud checks), cis (kube-bench), kube (kubescape NSA/MITRE), images (trivy), host (OpenSCAP CIS), stig (DISA STIG), cloud (prowler CIS), fips (FIPS 140 verification), all (security scans only), reports. Architecture returns PASS, FAIL, or INCOMPLETE when required evidence is missing or stale. Every kind except architecture, fips and reports runs cluster jobs or Ansible on hosts and needs confirm=true; a scanner missing on this machine is never installed by an MCP call (it stops with the install command for the user).

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `architecture` \| `cis` \| `kube` \| `images` \| `host` \| `stig` \| `cloud` \| `fips` \| `all` \| `reports` | yes |  |
| `cloud` | `aws` \| `gcp` \| `azure` \| `vmware` |  | target: aws &#124; gcp &#124; azure &#124; vmware |
| `env` | string |  | environment name, e.g. dev (lowercase letters, digits, hyphens). Blank: the cloud's only environment, else the current one for read-only tools, else dev; tools that change things never guess |
| `profile` | `production` \| `lab` \| `cis` \| `stig` |  | architecture: production (default) or lab; host/all: cis (default) or stig |
| `max_age_days` | integer |  | architecture: maximum age of saved evidence in days (default 30) |
| `json` | boolean |  | architecture: return the full assessment as JSON |
| `framework` | string |  |  |
| `hosts` | string |  | host/stig/all: comma-separated: bastion,vpn,k8s (default: every reachable host) |
| `confirm` | boolean |  | must be true to run a destructive action (ask the user first) |

### cloudseed_undo

Undo the newest state-changing action of an environment (fifteen kept per environment, at most five of one kind): restores the previous configuration and re-applies, uninstalls what was installed, revokes, deletes backups... list=true shows the history with entry ids; pass cloud (+ env), or the id of the newest entry of an environment. drop=true discards that entry without undoing it (for a step that can never succeed). Global actions (MCP/UI/credential/agent settings) can only be undone by the user (cs undo --global in a terminal, or the web console's Undo): an agent's call is refused. Everything except list=true needs confirm=true.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cloud` | `aws` \| `gcp` \| `azure` \| `vmware` |  | target: aws &#124; gcp &#124; azure &#124; vmware |
| `env` | string |  | environment name, e.g. dev (lowercase letters, digits, hyphens). Blank: the cloud's only environment, else the current one for read-only tools, else dev; tools that change things never guess |
| `id` | string |  | entry id from list=true (must be the newest of its environment) |
| `list` | boolean |  | show the history (with entry ids) instead of undoing |
| `drop` | boolean |  | discard the entry from the history without undoing it (nothing is changed) |
| `confirm` | boolean |  | must be true to run a destructive action (ask the user first) |

### cloudseed_install

Install a tool or group cloudseed needs: terraform aws gcloud az kubectl helm k9s openvpn tailscale go qemu-img vmware-provider &#124; cloud vmware vpn. Needs confirm=true (ask the user first).

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `what` | array of string | yes |  |
| `confirm` | boolean |  | must be true to run a destructive action (ask the user first) |

### cloudseed_skill

Read one of the bundled agent skills (cloudseed, cloudseed-aws/gcp/azure/vmware, cloudseed-destroy, cloudseed-platform, ...): the operating manual for driving cloudseed.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string |  | skill name, short or full (aws = cloudseed-aws, platform, destroy ...); empty = list them |

| Prompt | Arguments | Description |

| `create-environment` | `cloud`, `env` (optional), `region` (optional), `extras` (optional) | Plan and create a secure landing zone on a cloud, showing the plan before applying. |
| `review-environment` | `cloud`, `env` (optional) | Health, cost and security review of an existing environment. |
| `troubleshoot` | `cloud`, `env` (optional) | Diagnose the last failure in an environment and propose the fix. |
| `teardown` | `cloud`, `env` | Safely destroy an environment (restates what is deleted, asks for confirmation). |
